function: Excluded as above_phy: the learned safety-RL (CUP) policy outputs user weights for rate scheduling from buffer and delay states (p. 3); the precoder itself is the classical WMMSE (p. 9).
notes: Reason above_phy. p. 1: 'rate scheduling via a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP), and instantaneous precoding through weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization'. p. 3: the RL 'derive[s] user weights (action) reflecting priority in user rate scheduling, rather than high-dimensional beamforming matrices'. p. 8: the policy state is buffer delay and traffic bins plus the CSIT norm, and at inference 'only the policy network works, deriving the user weights'. p. 9-10: the precoder is computed by the non-learned WMMSE (Algorithm 3). p. 6: the WMMSE solution gives the bits per user 'before medium access control (MAC) executes FIFO scheduling', and the updated buffer drives the next weights. Borderline case: if the reviewer counts the learned weights as part of the precoder design, the area would be 3 and the marks q1 0 (custom Rayleigh simulator, p. 10), q2 0 (traffic sweep trained and tested per condition, p. 13), q3 0 (only learned baseline 'penalty' is a variant of CUP, p. 10), q4 1 (O(L_WMMSE,max N_bi U K Nt^3) and about 5,000 policy parameters, p. 10), q5 0 (no release).
